proposals.announcement_evidence: The basic Modular Mission Computer upgrade effort serves to resolve shortfalls in mission computer memory and throughput.
proposals.lexicon_quote: Modular Mission Computer (MMC)	0207133F	412	F-16 Squadrons
proposals.rationale: The announcement carries the index name verbatim (only the parenthetical acronym gloss is absent, so no alias inference is needed) and the named thing is the program itself, not a platform it supports: the contract's whole subject is the Modular Mission Computer upgrade, the F-16 mission computer built by Raytheon in McKinney, Texas, under AFLCMC's F-16 division at Wright-Patterson (FA8615). The action is developmental on its face — a cost-plus-fixed-fee modification definitizing four Remote Interface Panel change orders against an upgrade effort whose purpose is to resolve mission-computer memory and throughput shortfalls — which is the operational-systems-development content RDT&E PE 0207133F 'F-16 Squadrons' funds, and that PE is the only row in this index that owns the MMC name (its sibling F-16 procurement BLIs F01600 and F0160P carry AESA and AGCAS, not MMC). The weakness I record openly: no funds are obligated on this definitization, so the announcement gives no money colour of its own and the RDT&E attribution rests on the cost-plus contract type, the development purpose and the single index owner.

refute_a.reason: Money colour holds on lake evidence despite the announcement obligating nothing: all 129 lake rows for FA8615-17-C-6051 (2016-11-22 to 2025-12-23, $153,539,531 obligated, Raytheon) carry federal_accounts_funding_this_award = '057-3600' alone, and budget_lines puts 0207133F on account 3600F = 057-3600 (RDT&E, Air Force), so money_color_ok() returns True on an exact single-account match - the CPFF definitization of Remote Interface Panel change orders under the MMC upgrade is RDT&E work paid from the very appropriation that funds this line, not O&M sustainment hung on it; the named thing is the program itself (the Modular Mission Computer upgrade is the whole subject of the action, not an F-16 the contract merely supports), and PE 0207133F 'F-16 Squadrons' is a four-effort operational-systems-development line (APG-83, APX-127, IVEWS, MMC), not a rollup or a CATCHALL_TITLE aggregate.

refute_b.reason: "Modular Mission Computer (MMC)" is on exactly one index row (line 72, 0207133F) and "mission computer" appears nowhere else in F.tsv; the sibling F-16 procurement lines F01600/F0160P own only AESA and AGCAS, no MMC, so no alternative owner competes, the name is uttered verbatim (no alias to invent), and the FA8615 F-16 SPO number plus Raytheon McKinney — the F-16 MMC producer — fix the identity on the F-16 MMC rather than some other platform's mission computer.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle (EELV) Phase 1
proposals.lexicon_quote: The National Security Space Launch (NSSL)	NSSL00	416	National Security Space Launch
proposals.rationale: EELV is the former name of the same program and the same appropriation line: the Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle program was renamed National Security Space Launch in March 2019, so 'Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle (EELV) Phase 1' is a rename-alias of the index name rather than a different program (hence llm-alias, not exact-name). The award buys launch capability itself, not support to a platform — the modification 'provides for an increase in the mission resiliency for a launch vehicle configuration that had been previously ordered under the EELV contract' with United Launch Services, the EELV/NSSL Phase 1 launch provider, work at Centennial, Decatur and Cape Canaveral. The money colour resolves the index's NSSL collision: 'Fiscal 2018 space procurement funds in the amount of $18,866,624' are obligated, which belongs to the space procurement BLI NSSL00 (doc 416) and not to the RDT&E EMD line 1206853SF that carries the same name.

refute_a.reason: REFUTED on appropriation: budget_lines carries exactly one account for NSSL00 - 3022F = 057-3022, the Space Force's own procurement appropriation (its P-1 siblings on 3022F are the Space Force lines) - while all 156 lake rows for FA8811-13-C-0003 (including P00192 itself, 2018-05-11, $18,866,842) carry federal_accounts_funding_this_award = '017-1507;057-3020;057-3021;057-3600', i.e. Missile Procurement AF, Space Procurement AF and RDT&E AF, with 057-3022 absent, so the announcement's 'fiscal 2018 space procurement funds' are Air Force space/missile procurement dollars and not one cent of the appropriation that funds the line named here; I ran the loader's own guard - money_color_ok({017-1507,057-3020,057-3021,057-3600}, {057-3022}) is False, so this link would be counted skipped['money_color_mismatch'] and could never publish, and the index offers no money-colour-compatible alternative either (the sibling NSSL row 1206853SF sits on 3620F = 057-3620, RDT&E Space Force, equally disjoint).

refute_b.reason: A real collision exists — the identical string "The National Security Space Launch (NSSL)" is also on 1206853SF (doc 417, "NSSL Program (SPACE) - EMD") — but the evidence does not link there equally well: the announcement obligates "fiscal 2018 space procurement funds" for added mission resiliency on an already-ordered Phase 1 launch vehicle configuration, which is procurement of launch capability, not EMD work or a Launch Service Agreement, and the EELV→NSSL rename (2019) is a documented rename of this same line, not an invented alias or a different increment (EELV appears on no index row, so no third owner competes).

proposals.announcement_evidence: Base Expeditionary Airfield Resources (BEAR) kitchens program
proposals.lexicon_quote: Basic Expeditionary Airfield Resources (BEAR)	845420	411	Mobility Equipment
proposals.rationale: The acronym is identical and only one word of the expansion differs ('Base' for 'Basic'), a routine variant of the same program name, which is why this is llm-alias rather than exact-name; BEAR appears on exactly one row of this index, so no other PE competes for it. The deliverable IS the line's own content, not a platform it supports: 'The BEAR kitchens are modular, deployable kitchens with the electrical and water systems to connect to the BEAR power grid and water distribution systems,' i.e. BEAR set equipment bought for deployed airfield basing, which is what the Other Procurement AF line item 845420 (doc 411, 'Mobility Equipment') funds, and the requirements-type indefinite-delivery contract is a supply vehicle for that equipment rather than a services or construction award. The caveat I record: 'No funds' are obligated at award, so the announcement states no appropriation and the procurement colour is inferred from the equipment nature of the buy and the BEAR line's own content.

refute_a.reason: The appropriation question, which the announcement leaves open ('No funds are being obligated at the time of award. Individual delivery orders will be issued'), is answered affirmatively by the lake: the 12 delivery orders whose parent_award_id_piid is FA8533-15-D-0001 obligate $68,511,147 and every one carries federal account 057-3080 = Other Procurement, Air Force, exactly the 3080F account budget_lines gives BLI 845420, so the work ordered through this vehicle executed this line's own money rather than O&M (the expense-funded field-catering alternative I tested for), and the FPDS product code 'SETS, KITS, OUTFITS AND MODULES, FOOD PREPERATION AND SERVING' confirms an equipment buy, not services or construction; mission fits too - BEAR set kitchens that plug into the BEAR power grid and water distribution are the line's own named item, not a platform the contract supports, and 'Mobility Equipment' is a five-item equipment line (BEAR, EALS, MAAS, RALS, ROWPU) that CATCHALL_TITLE does not match. Weakness recorded openly: the vehicle row itself obligates $0 across all 11 of its own lake transactions, so 'this action paid for the line's work' rests on its orders' money, and the published Related Awards row will show $0 on this PIID.

refute_b.reason: BEAR is on exactly one index row (line 961, 845420); the only other "expeditionary airfield" rows are EALS on the same BLI and an unrelated "Deployable C3 Expeditionary Airfield Basing Assets ISSP" under 861900, which shares no name with this award, and the "Base" vs "Basic" expansion is a one-word variant of the same acronym and program rather than an invented alias — the announcement itself ties the kitchens to the BEAR power grid and water distribution systems, so it is the BEAR set's own equipment, not a different increment and not merely the contractor's name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Air Force Subscale Aerial Target (AFSAT) Lots 11-13 production
proposals.lexicon_quote: BQM-167A	10TRGT	407	Target Drones
proposals.rationale: AFSAT is the program name of the BQM-167A itself — the Air Force Subscale Aerial Target is the BQM-167A airframe, produced by Composite Engineering (Kratos) in Sacramento, which is exactly the awardee and place of performance here — so the index row's designator and the announcement's program name denote one thing (llm-alias). The action is production, not development: 'additional quantity of 21 AFSAT production units being produced under the basic contract (Lot 12) and the associated warranty,' with 'Fiscal 2016 procurement funds in the amount of $17,785,195 are being obligated at the time of award.' Procurement money for production units belongs to the aircraft procurement BLI 10TRGT 'Target Drones' (doc 407), which buys the subscale targets, rather than to the RDT&E PE 0305116F 'Aerial Targets' that also carries the BQM-167A name and whose AFSAT row is explicitly the *Development* effort — I propose that row separately as weak so the collision is on the ledger. 'Target Drones' is a two-name equipment line (BQM-167A, QF-16), not a catch-all rollup.

refute_a.reason: Money colour matches exactly and settles the RDT&E/procurement collision in the proposal's favour: the announcement obligates 'fiscal 2016 procurement funds in the amount of $17,785,195', all 26 lake rows for FA8678-15-C-0069 ($25,177,539 obligated, Kratos Unmanned Aerial Systems, product code 'UNMANNED AIRCRAFT') carry federal_accounts_funding_this_award = '057-3010', and budget_lines puts 10TRGT on 3010F = 057-3010 (Aircraft Procurement, Air Force), so money_color_ok() is True on a single-account match while the rival RDT&E owner of the same name (0305116F 'Aerial Targets', account 3600F = 057-3600) is disjoint from every dollar on this contract; the scope is production - 21 AFSAT production units under Lot 12 plus warranty - which is the procurement line's own content, the target drone is the end item and not a platform being supported, and 'Target Drones' carries only BQM-167A and QF-16, so it is no rollup.

refute_b.reason: The collision is real and worse than usual — 0305116F (doc 412, "Aerial Targets") owns BOTH the announcement's literal phrase, as "AF Subscale Aerial Target (AFSAT) Development", and the proposal's chosen designator BQM-167A — yet the evidence does not link there equally well: that row is explicitly the *Development* effort on an RDT&E program element, while this action buys "21 AFSAT production units ... (Lot 12)" with "fiscal 2016 procurement funds", which an RDT&E PE's work cannot consume, and 10TRGT is the only procurement row for a subscale target (its sibling QF-16 is the full-scale target); the AFSAT=BQM-167A equivalence is real and independently corroborated by the awardee, Composite Engineering of Sacramento, the BQM-167A producer, and Lots 11-13 are lots of that same variant, not a different one.

Mission fits the line and is not sustainment: an 'expanded command and control developmental system to integrate sensor data, manage effects, and execute command and control', a period-of-performance extension on a developmental contract, which is exactly the development content an RDT&E line funds; DBMN is the thing being built (PE 0604003F's narrative owns it, and the announcement names the parent ABMS in the same clause), not a platform the contract merely supports, and ABMS is a named program element with eight named efforts rather than a catch-all aggregate.

refute_b.reason: Both "Distributable Battle Management Node (DBMN)" and "Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS)" sit only on 0604003F (lines 429 and 432), and the announcement names both in one clause, so there is no alternative owner and no alias inference at all; the only similarly-worded index entries are DBMA on the same PE (harmless) and TBMCS under 834530, which shares no name with this award, and "Phase 1" is the first increment of this same named node rather than a different program or variant.
